title: Implement object-history-03 (sub-epic: history get, restore, destroyed query)
description:
Design: docs/design/object-history.md. Decisions: docs/design/DECISIONS.md.
Note key: E. Crates: jmap-object-history-types/-server/-client (new); jmap-types; jmap-server; mail, contacts, calendars, filenode, tasks, chat, graph, scene, vtc -types/-server; jmap-testjig. Size: L.

Convert JMAP-tna1.3 into the object-history sub-epic of JMAP-tna1. Design: docs/design/object-history.md (final); decisions in docs/design/DECISIONS.md (5 scope, 6 stopgaps, 14 shared registry; also 1, 4, 7, 8, 10, 11). Spec: ~/PROJECT/IETF/specs/draft-ietf-jmap-object-history-03.xml.

Scope (decision 5): the 11 Table 1 'Supports History: Yes' types, plus Task/TaskList, plus Mark's private types. Chat: Chat, Message, Space, ChatContact, CustomEmoji, SpaceBan, SpaceInvite. Graph: Graph, GraphNode, GraphEdge. Scene: SceneAsset, SceneRegion, SceneObject. VTC: VTCCall, VTCRecording, VTCLivestream. Excluded (decision 22, D1 closed): GraphNodeOp, PresenceStatus, ReadPosition, SceneAvatar, VTCParticipant, TaskNotification, KeyPackage. Task/TaskList registrations come from Mark's own Tasks draft (decision 23, JMAP-jkl8.9).

Approach: opt-in through a separate ObjectHistoryBackend trait and register_<x>_handlers_with_history per crate. Plain handlers stay unchanged (decision 1 adopts this pattern). The four spec-gap stopgaps are implemented now and raised upstream (decision 6).

Children and order are in note §11. Done when all children are closed and testjig serves the spec examples end to end with no object_history_gaps.
notes:
Decision Mark 2026-11-12: crate-jmap aims to be THE complete reference implementation covering the JMAP specs, so this is required work, not optional. Split rule: the crates own wire types, validation, method semantics and error mapping; storage-, transport- or media-specific work is pushed to the calling crate through backend trait hooks (see the spec-method-defaults memory: no no-op default when that would put wrong data on the wire). Here: method semantics in the crates; history retention and storage are backend hooks.
